title: Computer Graphics
tagline: Images and colour, transformations, viewing and projection, rasterisation, shading, texture mapping, the GPU pipeline, ray tracing, curves and animation
summary: Computer graphics turns geometric descriptions of a scene into images. This course covers raster images and colour, transformations with homogeneous coordinates, cameras and projection, rasterisation and visibility, lighting, shading and texture mapping, the programmable GPU pipeline, ray tracing and global illumination, and curves, surfaces and animation.

chapters.title: Raster images and colour
chapters.summary: Pixels and sampling, colour spaces and gamma, and aliasing.

chapters.title: Transformations
chapters.summary: 2D and 3D transformations, homogeneous coordinates and composing transformations.

chapters.title: Viewing and projection
chapters.summary: Cameras, orthographic and perspective projection, and the viewing pipeline.

chapters.title: Rasterisation and visibility
chapters.summary: Drawing lines and triangles, barycentric interpolation, clipping and the depth buffer.

chapters.title: Lighting and shading
chapters.summary: How light interacts with surfaces, the Phong and physically based models, and smooth shading.

chapters.title: Texture mapping
chapters.summary: Texture coordinates, filtering and mipmapping, and bump and environment mapping.

chapters.title: The GPU pipeline and shaders
chapters.summary: The programmable pipeline, vertex and fragment shaders, and real-time rendering techniques.

chapters.title: Ray tracing and global illumination
chapters.summary: Ray–object intersection, acceleration structures, the rendering equation and path tracing.

chapters.title: Curves, surfaces and animation
chapters.summary: Bézier curves and splines, subdivision surfaces, keyframing and skeletal animation.
